submissions.head: Afloat16:fix/ndcg-gain-range-20261116
submissions.title: Preserve NDCG ratios across finite gain scales
submissions.body:
## Problem

NDCG can return NaN even when every custom gain is finite: gains [1.5, 1.3, 1.0] scaled by 1e308 overflow the discounted sums. At subnormal gain scales, accumulating before taking the ratio also loses information that remains representable in the normalized score.

## Change

Normalize the actual and ideal gain vectors by the same per-class scale before discounting. Choose that scale after self-exclusion and ideal top-k selection, then retain the existing zero-ideal convention and pooled/per-class aggregation.

- Unchanged production base `b95a423`: 16 regression failures and 20 passing controls.
- All 90 focused and adjacent tests pass; 2 device-specific cases deselected. 36 new cases use a 100-digit Decimal ratio computed from the actual quantized gain inputs. They cover large, ordinary, and subnormal scales; ranking order; cutoff depth; self-exclusion; pooled and per-class registered metrics; and empty or zero-ideal controls.
- Full CPU suite: 1,565 passed; 10 device-specific tests deselected.

submissions.name: p2s-center-precision
submissions.head: Afloat16:fix/p2s-center-precision-20261116
submissions.title: Preserve P2SGrad learning signals close to class centers
submissions.body:
## Problem

For an embedding close to its target class center, low-precision cosine multiplication rounds the cosine to 1 before P2SGrad forms the squared residual. For example, [1, 0.02] against [1, 0] produces zero loss and zero training gradients in float16/bfloat16 and under CPU autocast, although the squared residual is about 4e-8 and the parameter gradient is representable.

## Change

Keep embedding normalization, cosine multiplication, and mean-squared residuals in the accumulation dtype, with autocast disabled for the cosine calculation. Preserve the original normalization epsilon, in-place no-grad center normalization, public scalar dtype outside autocast, and autocast's float32 MSE result.

## Validation

- Unchanged production base `b95a423`: 12 regression failures and 15 passing controls.
- All 47 focused and adjacent tests pass. 27 new cases compare values, embedding gradients, and parameter gradients against independent float64 equations across four dtypes, multiple near-center offsets, and one/two class centers. They also verify optimizer updates, autocast behavior, and the existing float16 normalization epsilon.
- Full CPU suite: 1,556 passed; 10 device-specific tests deselected.

submissions.name: circle-weight-precision
submissions.head: Afloat16:fix/circle-weight-precision-20261116
submissions.title: Keep CircleLoss adaptive-weight arithmetic finite before reduction
submissions.body:
## Problem

CircleLoss can overflow its detached adaptive weights before multiplying them by a zero boundary residual. With float16, margin 0.5, gamma 100000, and selected similarities 0.5, the expected finite loss is log(3), but the current path returns zero with NaN gradients. Large opposite positive/negative logit offsets can also discard log-count terms or perturb the logsumexp gradient before the two partitions are combined.

## Change

Evaluate the adaptive weights and logit products in the accumulation dtype. Center the selected positive and negative partitions separately, combine their detached shifts before adding the centered log-sums, and retain the original output dtype and detached-weight objective.

## Validation

[Exact-base and independent-candidate validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43859155299/job/133271104426):

- Unchanged production base `b95a423`: 12 regression failures and 20 passing controls.
- All 89 focused and adjacent tests pass. The 32 new cases verify closed-form boundary values and matrix gradients across four dtypes, margins, and gamma values; rectangular reference batches; missing-pair controls; and exactly cancelling logit offsets of magnitude 37,500,000. The latter retain log(3) and analytic gradients without loosening existing numerical tolerances.
- Full CPU suite: 1,561 passed; 10 device-specific tests deselected.

submissions.name: large-vector-normalization
submissions.head: Afloat16:fix/large-vector-normalization-20261116
submissions.title: Preserve normalized directions and gradients for large finite embeddings
submissions.body:
## Problem

Normalizing a finite vector can return an all-zero direction and zero gradients when the intermediate power sum overflows. For example, cosine similarity between float32 [3e20, 4e20] and [1, 0] returns 0 instead of 0.6, despite the true norm and normalized direction being finite. The same issue reaches both matrix and pairwise distance paths.

## Change

Before norm accumulation, scale only vectors whose largest component exceeds the safe power-sum bound derived from their accumulation dtype, norm order, and dimension. Compute normalization in that scaled space and adjust the epsilon by the same scale. Ordinary vectors retain their existing values and gradients exactly, including in mixed batches; empty dimensions, norm orders below one, and the infinity norm keep the existing path.

## Validation

- Unchanged production base `b95a423`: 17 regression failures and 39 passing controls.
- All 187 focused and adjacent tests pass, including the existing ProxyNCA and TupletMargin value/gradient contracts. The 56 new cases use 100-digit Decimal normalization and analytic gradients across four dtypes, norm orders 1/2/3/infinity, and both axes; check matrix/pairwise cosine paths and empty shapes; and require exact ordinary-input values and gradients.
- Full CPU suite: 1,585 passed; 10 device-specific tests deselected.

history_refresh.body:
## Problem

IntraPairVariance rounds the selected-pair mean in float16/bfloat16 before subtracting it. Widen selected float16/bfloat16 pair values before their mean, epsilon adjustment, and squared hinge. history_refresh.title: Preserve decoupled contrastive objectives across large score offsets
history_refresh.body:

DCL subtracts an absolute positive score from an absolute negative log-partition. With four equal float32 scores at 1e8, this cancellation returns zero instead of log(2). Dividing large finite scores by a small temperature can also overflow before normalization and silently discard valid anchors.

history_refresh.title: Keep DynamicArcFace class margins finite across count and power ranges
history_refresh.body:
## Problem

DynamicArcFace normalizes inverse powers of class counts by their absolute range. Distinct counts such as [10, 100, 1000] with power = 1000 or 1e-20 produce a zero range and NaN margins. Adjacent int64 counts above 2^53 can also collapse when converted to floating point before their differences are formed. The invalid margins propagate into training.

## Change

Evaluate the normalized power-law range from relative logarithms and stable exponential differences. Form integer count differences before converting to float64, and use the analytic small-span limit when normalization would otherwise divide subnormal values. Preserve the configured margin endpoints, scale invariance, and class ordering. Reject nonfinite powers as well as nonpositive powers.

## Validation

- Unchanged production base `b95a423`: 25 regression failures and 11 passing controls.

A 400-digit Decimal power-law reference checks the configured endpoints and intermediate margins across four count ranges, three powers, and two margin intervals. history_refresh.body:

SoftTriple divides each center similarity by gamma before computing the center softmax. Widen float16/bfloat16 center similarities before the weighting arithmetic and remove the maximum within each class before dividing by gamma. Each class retains its own normalization; the public logits retain their original absolute scale.

history_refresh.title: Preserve PNP ranking penalties and gradients near zero
history_refresh.body:
## Problem

The PNP variant transforms can erase or distort small soft-ranking penalties after the sigmoid has computed them correctly. For a valid cosine-similarity matrix with positive similarity 0.95, negative similarity 0.65, and the default temperature 0.01, float32 Ds/Dq/Iu losses become zero. Ib returns about 4.71e-14 instead of 8.76e-27 and drops a nonzero gradient. The issue also affects double precision and representable low-precision penalties.

Use log1p for logarithmic increments and negative expm1 for each Dq penalty before averaging. Evaluate the Ib transform with its small-argument series near zero, masking the unused polynomial input to avoid overflow in backward. Widen float16/bfloat16 similarities before ranking arithmetic, then preserve the existing returned scalar dtype. The variant objectives, sigmoid temperature, and API stay the same.

history_refresh.title: Preserve weighted triplet sampling across finite weight scales
history_refresh.body:
## Problem

Weighted triplet sampling casts the negative weights to float32 before masking and sampling. Finite double weights can therefore underflow to zero or overflow to infinity. The latter also creates `0 * inf` in masked positive/self positions. Rows with valid positive-weight negatives then silently produce no triplets: a common weight scale of either 1e-50 or 1e50 reproduces the problem.

## Change

Mask ineligible entries first and rescale each row by its largest eligible weight before converting to the sampling dtype. This preserves relative probabilities and keeps zero-weight rows empty, including empty comparison axes. The input weights are not mutated. Document that exact seeded weighted draws may change as a consequence of the rescaling, and register the regression file in the numerical focused suite.

history_refresh.title: Preserve ArcFace gradients through linear target-logit branches
history_refresh.body:
## Problem

ArcFace reconstructs the target cosine with `cos(acos(clamp(cosine)))` even in its linear monotonic continuation. When floating-point rounding places the cosine at an endpoint, this path loses the target-cosine derivative. A zero margin also loses the identity derivative through the same round trip.

For a float16 embedding `[1, 0.01]`, class weights `[[1, 0], [-1, 0]]`, and target class 1, the target weight receives no gradient and the embedding directional gradient is halved. With zero margin and scale 1, the current directional gradient is approximately `-0.008804`, versus the independent cosine cross-entropy reference `-0.017617`. The same defect occurs in the normal margin-0.5 continuation and in float32/float64 examples whose target cosines round to an endpoint.

## Change

Use the original target cosine in the monotonic continuation and return it directly for zero margins. The angular branch and its switch retain their current definition. SubCenterArcFaceLoss and DynamicArcFaceLoss inherit the correction, including class-specific zero margins. Update the component documentation, numerical rationale, and unreleased notes.

## Validation

[Independent validation on the exact base and corrected tree](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43844314617/job/133220519659):

- Unchanged production base `b95a423`: 25 regression failures and 9 passing controls; one unrelated test deselected by the focused selection.
- All 51 ArcFace, SubCenterArcFace, and DynamicArcFace tests pass after the fix. The regressions check target-logit derivatives and compare actual embedding/proxy gradients against an independent cosine cross-entropy reference across float16, float32, and float64.
- Full CPU suite: 1,563 passed; 10 device-specific tests deselected.

history_refresh.title: Preserve finite scaled logits in LargeMarginSoftmax and SphereFace
history_refresh.body:
## Problem

`LargeMarginSoftmaxLoss` and `SphereFaceLoss` form embedding norms in the input dtype before scaling their cosine logits. With float16 inputs, an intermediate norm can overflow even when the final logits and training gradients are representable. For example, a one-row embedding `[60000, 60000]` with weights `0.5 * I` and margin 1 has LargeMarginSoftmax logits `[30000, 30000]` and loss `log(2)`, but currently produces infinite logits and non-finite training gradients. SphereFace has the same norm overflow with finite expected logits `[60000, 60000]`.

LargeMarginSoftmax also multiplies the embedding and weight norms before applying the cosine and scale. This product can overflow, or underflow to zero before a larger scale restores a representable value, dropping a real training gradient.

## Change

Compute low-precision norms and the complete magnitude/cosine/scale product in float32, then return logits in the dtype selected by the original operands. Float32 and float64 retain their precision, and mixed-input/autocast promotion is preserved. The change covers both losses in one patch because they share the same norm-scaling calculation.

The cosine calculation, angular-margin polynomial, normalization epsilon, and final logit dtype are unchanged. The fix does not extend the final dtype's range or promise finite gradients when the existing cosine or margin computation itself exceeds its precision or range. The docs and release notes describe these boundaries.

Compute low-precision differences, variances, and their ratio in float32, sharing the calculation between the matrix and pairwise paths. Convert only the final ratio to the existing result dtype. Float32 and float64 inputs are not narrowed, and the normalization and output-dtype contracts stay intact.

The component docs and release notes describe the precision behavior. Truly zero query variance remains undefined, normalization rounding is unchanged, and ratios outside the result dtype's range can still overflow.

history_refresh.body:
## Summary

A common bias should cancel in GE2ELoss's softmax objective, but adding it to every logit can round away class differences.
